question: Can the first player force the Snaky shape on an infinite board?
idea: Two players alternate claiming empty squares. The manuscript claims the first player can guarantee the six-square Snaky pattern within twenty-one of their own moves, whatever the opponent does. Translations, rotations and reflections all count as the same winning shape under these rules.
why: The study of arrangements, networks, and counting. It looks for patterns that must appear when a structure is large or dense enough.
exactClaim: Settles the Snaky achievement problem: Maker can force the six-cell Snaky shape within 21 of its own moves on the initially empty infinite square board. Maker moves first, each player claims one free cell per turn, and translations, rotations and reflections count as wins. )
reviewStatus: assistant-authored from source summary; not mathematically reviewed
scope: Family-level introduction based on the pinned catalogue summary. Summarizes manuscript claims; not an independent proof review.
